blocks.content: A second appeal against the decision shall lie within ninety days from the date on which the decision should have been made or was actually received.

rows: First Appellate Authority (Senior Officer in same Dept)
No explicit statutory cap (decided by Commission)
No power to fine PIO under Sec 20
Can impose fines up to ₹25,000 on PIO

items: Crucial distinction: First Appeal goes to an internal departmental officer (FAA), whereas Second Appeal goes to an independent statutory body (CIC/SIC).
Maximum monetary penalty on an errant PIO is capped at ₹25,000 under Section 20.
Information concerning life or liberty must be provided within 48 hours, failing which direct appeal pathways open up.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: First Appeal is filed before an officer senior in rank to the CPIO/SPIO within 30 days of receiving the response or expiry of the deadline.
The First Appellate Authority (FAA) must dispose of the appeal within 30 days, extendable to a maximum of 45 days with written justification.
Second Appeal lies with the Central Information Commission (CIC) or State Information Commission (SIC) within 90 days of the FAA order.
Under Section 20(1) of the RTI Act 2005, penalty up to ₹250 per day (subject to a maximum of ₹25,000) can be imposed on a PIO for failing to provide information without reasonable cause.
The burden of proving that he or she acted reasonably and diligently lies entirely on the Public Information Officer.
